methodology: GST explanations checked against CBIC Tax Information Portal and GST Portal. Verify amendments, notifications and rules applicable to the tax period.

3008.title: Input Tax Credit: basic GST mechanism
3008.overview: ITC is eligible GST paid on inward supplies used or intended for business and credited against output tax liability, subject to statutory conditions.
3008.context: GST reduces cascading: a registered business pays tax on purchases and collects tax on taxable outward supplies.
3008.who: The claimant must be registered and the inward goods/services must be used or intended for business, subject to the Act.
3008.what: Section 16 requires prescribed documents, supplier-furnished details communicated to the recipient, receipt of goods/services, payment of tax to Government and return compliance. Section 17 restricts non-business/exempt use and blocks specified credits.
3008.why: These checks protect the credit chain and prevent claims on fictitious, unreceived or ineligible purchases.
3008.significance: ITC is a statutory credit, not automatic. Check invoice, supplier reporting, receipt, tax payment, return filing and blocked-credit rules.
3008.exam: Legal anchor: CGST Act, 2017, Sections 16 and 17. Verify amendments and notifications for the tax period.
3008.source: CBIC Tax Information Portal; statutory text checked 4 November 2026.

5038.title: Intra-State supply: CGST with SGST/UTGST
5038.overview: A normal taxable intra-State supply is generally subject to CGST plus SGST, or CGST plus UTGST where the UTGST law applies.
5038.context: GST uses a dual levy within a State/UT and an integrated levy for inter-State supplies.
5038.who: The supplier's location and place of supply are the starting points for classification.
5038.what: CGST is levied under CGST Act Section 9; the corresponding SGST/UTGST is levied under applicable law. Inter-State supplies are generally subject to IGST.
5038.why: Correct classification determines the tax head and avoids short payment or wrong-head payment.
5038.significance: Example: at a total 18% rate on ₹10,000, the usual split is CGST ₹900 and SGST/UTGST ₹900, assuming equal split and no special rule.
5038.exam: Legal anchor: CGST Act Section 9 and IGST Act Section 8; check place-of-supply rules and exceptions.

5039.title: Why Input Tax Credit matters
5039.overview: ITC allows eligible tax on business inputs to be credited against output GST, reducing cascading. Example: output GST ₹1,800 less eligible ITC ₹900 leaves ₹900 net liability before other adjustments.
5039.context: GST reduces cascading: a registered business pays tax on purchases and collects tax on taxable outward supplies.
5039.who: The claimant must be registered and the inward goods/services must be used or intended for business, subject to the Act.
5039.what: Section 16 requires prescribed documents, supplier-furnished details communicated to the recipient, receipt of goods/services, payment of tax to Government and return compliance. Section 17 restricts non-business/exempt use and blocks specified credits.
5039.why: These checks protect the credit chain and prevent claims on fictitious, unreceived or ineligible purchases.
5039.significance: ITC is a statutory credit, not automatic. Check invoice, supplier reporting, receipt, tax payment, return filing and blocked-credit rules.
5039.exam: ITC is not an unconditional refund; Sections 16 and 17 govern eligibility and restrictions.
5039.source: CBIC Tax Information Portal; statutory text checked 4 November 2026.

5085.title: GST: Goods and Services Tax
5085.overview: GST stands for Goods and Services Tax, an indirect tax on supply of goods and services in India.
5085.context: The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 enabled the GST framework; GST commenced on 1 July 2017.
5085.who: Union and State/UT governments administer components through the statutory framework and GST Council recommendations.
5085.what: CGST, SGST/UTGST and IGST apply according to nature and place of supply.
5085.why: GST replaced many earlier indirect levies with a harmonised supply-based framework and ITC chain.
5085.significance: For tax-office work, learn the taxable event (supply), direct/indirect tax distinction and intra-State/inter-State components.
5085.exam: GST is not a tax on income or profit; it is an indirect tax on supply.

5086.title: GSTR-1: outward-supply reporting
5086.overview: GSTR-1 is the statement in which a registered supplier reports prescribed details of outward supplies for a tax period.
5086.context: Outward supplies are supplies made by the taxpayer; their details support recipient invoice visibility and liability reconciliation.
5086.who: The registered supplier furnishes GSTR-1 subject to the applicable filing scheme.
5086.what: It includes prescribed invoice, credit/debit note, export and amendment details. GSTR-3B is a separate summary return.
5086.why: Accurate data supports invoice-level reporting, recipient visibility and reconciliation with books and GSTR-3B.
5086.significance: Reconcile taxable value and tax head-wise, review amendments and confirm the correct period.
5086.exam: Legal anchor: CGST Act Section 37 and applicable rules/notifications; check current due dates and tables.

6128.title: GSTIN: the 15-character identification number
6128.overview: A GSTIN is a 15-character alphanumeric identification number assigned to a registered person.
6128.context: Its structure uses State/UT code and PAN, followed by entity and check characters.
6128.who: The GST Portal assigns the GSTIN on registration.
6128.what: Standard structure: first 2 characters—State/UT code; next 10—PAN; 13th—entity number for that PAN in that State; 14th—normally Z; 15th—check digit.
6128.why: The structure identifies taxpayer and registration jurisdiction and distinguishes registrations linked to one PAN.
6128.significance: Verify GSTIN on the GST Portal before relying on supplier registration details.
6128.exam: GSTIN is 15 characters and alphanumeric, not simply a 15-digit number.

6196.title: IGST on inter-State supplies
6196.overview: IGST is generally levied on inter-State supplies of goods or services or both.
6196.context: Classification applies the location-of-supplier and place-of-supply rules.
6196.who: Supplier, recipient and place of supply must be identified; special rules apply to goods, services, imports, exports and SEZ supplies.
6196.what: IGST Act Section 5 is the charging provision; Section 7 sets out inter-State supply rules.
6196.why: Correct classification routes tax through the integrated mechanism and supports settlement between Union and States.
6196.significance: A supplier in Meghalaya supplying goods to a recipient in Assam will generally make an inter-State supply, subject to place-of-supply rules and exceptions.
6196.exam: Legal anchor: IGST Act Sections 5 and 7 and Chapter V. Do not classify only by billing address.
6196.source: CBIC GST Acts and GST Council.

6244.title: Reconciling GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B differences
6244.overview: GSTR-1 is the outward-supply statement; GSTR-3B is a summary return. A difference is a reconciliation signal, not proof of evasion by itself.
6244.context: Differences may arise from timing, amendments, credit/debit notes, tax-head classification, reverse charge, exports/SEZ, advances or data-entry errors.
6244.who: Reconcile books, GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, e-invoice data where applicable and tax ledgers; document period and tax-head comparison.
6244.what: Compare taxable value and CGST, SGST/UTGST and IGST separately. Identify invoices/notes causing the difference, obtain an explanation and check whether correction or payment is required.
6244.why: A disciplined reconciliation separates genuine reporting differences from short-reported liability and creates an auditable trail.
6244.significance: Example: ₹5,00,000 in GSTR-1 versus ₹4,80,000 in GSTR-3B is initially a ₹20,000 taxable-value difference, not ₹20,000 tax. Identify the rate and transaction cause first.
6244.exam: Legal anchor: CGST Act Sections 37, 39 and 61 and CGST Rules Rule 99; follow ASMT-10/11 where applicable and do not demand solely from a headline mismatch.
6244.source: CBIC and GST Portal return guidance.
